---
name: Ansible Eco vCenter Integration Test
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - "release-\\d.\\d"

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  prepare_matrix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # this environment requires approval to prevent abuse of the vCenter lab. It is used on this stage so you
    # only need to approve the workflow once, and then can re-run the jobs if there are failures. If new changes
    # are pushed, approval is required again.
    environment: eco-vcenter
    outputs:
      groups: ${{ steps.set-matrix.outputs.groups }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Check out into the collection path so ansible-test resolves the
          # collection, and fetch full history so --changed can diff against base.
          path: ansible_collections/vmware/vmware
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install ansible-core
        run: pip install ansible-core

      - name: List affected integration targets
        id: list-targets
        working-directory: ansible_collections/vmware/vmware
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # Global paths affect every target (or ansible-test cannot model them),
          # so a change to any of these forces the full suite to run. Note the
          # shared prepare_test_vars setup role is pulled in via meta/main.yml
          # dependencies, which ansible-test change detection does not follow.
          GLOBAL_RE='^(\.github/|Makefile$|tests/integration/(requirements|generate_integration_config|integration_config)|tests/integration/targets/prepare_test_vars/)'

          run_all=false
          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" != "pull_request_target" ]; then
            # Pushes to official branches: ansible-test refuses change detection
            # against an official branch, so run everything.
            run_all=true
          else
            # Make the base branch available locally for both the diff below and
            # ansible-test's --base-branch.
            git fetch origin "${BASE_REF}:refs/remotes/origin/${BASE_REF}"
            if git diff --name-only "origin/${BASE_REF}...HEAD" | grep -qE "${GLOBAL_RE}"; then
              run_all=true
            fi
          fi

          if [ "${run_all}" = "true" ]; then
            echo "Running all integration targets."
            ansible-test integration --list-targets > targets.txt
          else
            echo "Detecting integration targets changed against ${BASE_REF}."
            # Recreate the base branch locally so --base-branch can resolve it.
            git branch -f "${BASE_REF}" "origin/${BASE_REF}"
            git checkout -B "pr-${PR_NUMBER}"
            ansible-test integration --list-targets --changed \
              --base-branch "${BASE_REF}" > targets.txt
          fi

          echo "Selected targets:"
          cat targets.txt
        env:
          GITHUB_EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}

      - name: Build target groups matrix
        id: set-matrix
        working-directory: ansible_collections/vmware/vmware
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 << 'PY'
          import json
          import os

          # Skip helper roles (e.g. prepare_test_vars) and targets that must be
          # run manually (prefixed with "manual_").
          skip = {"prepare_test_vars"}
          with open("targets.txt", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
              targets = sorted(
                  name
                  for name in (line.strip() for line in fh)
                  if name
                  and name not in skip
                  and not name.startswith("manual_")
              )
          chunk = 5
          groups = [
              {"group": i // chunk, "targets": " ".join(targets[i : i + chunk])}
              for i in range(0, len(targets), chunk)
          ]
          with open(os.environ["GITHUB_OUTPUT"], "a", encoding="utf-8") as gh_out:
              gh_out.write(
                  "groups<<JSON_GROUPS_EOF\n"
                  f"{json.dumps(groups)}\n"
                  "JSON_GROUPS_EOF\n"
              )
          PY
        env:
          PYTHONIOENCODING: utf-8

  ansible_integration_test:
    runs-on: ["self-hosted", linux, X64]
    needs: prepare_matrix
    if: needs.prepare_matrix.outputs.groups != '[]'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJson(needs.prepare_matrix.outputs.groups) }}
    steps:
      - name: Echo group members
        run: |
          # this list is hard to see in the Github UI
          echo "${{ matrix.group }}"

      - name: Update pip, git
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && startsWith(runner.name, 'ubuntu')
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install podman

      - name: Checkout repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true

      - name: Generate integration config
        run: |
          make tests/integration/integration_config.yml
        env:
          VCENTER_HOSTNAME: ${{ secrets.VCENTER_HOSTNAME }}
          VCENTER_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.VCENTER_USERNAME }}
          VCENTER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.VCENTER_PASSWORD }}

      - name: Run integration tests (group ${{ matrix.group }})
        run: |
          python3 -m venv .venv
          source .venv/bin/activate
          make integration INTEGRATION_TARGETS='${{ matrix.targets }}'
        env:
          ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_PATH: "${{ github.workspace }}"
          VCENTER_HOSTNAME: ${{ secrets.VCENTER_HOSTNAME }}
          VCENTER_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.VCENTER_USERNAME }}
          VCENTER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.VCENTER_PASSWORD }}

      - name: Clean working directory
        if: always()
        run: |
          rm -rf ./*

  # This job does nothing and is only used for the branch protection
  # or multi-stage CI jobs, like making sure that all tests pass before
  # a publishing job is started.
  integration-check:
    if: always()
    needs:
      - ansible_integration_test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether the needed jobs succeeded or failed
        uses: re-actors/alls-green@release/v1
        with:
          # The test job is skipped when change detection selects no targets;
          # a skip must not fail branch protection.
          allowed-skips: ansible_integration_test
          jobs: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}

# https://github.com/ansible-collections/partner-certification-checker/blob/main/.ansible-lint

# https://docs.ansible.com/projects/lint/rules/sanity/, create a sanity ignore file

  certification_check:
    uses: ansible-collections/partner-certification-checker/.github/workflows/certification-reusable.yml@v5.0.0 # zizmor: ignore[unpinned-uses]
    # If the minimal Ansible Core version your collection supports Ansible
    # is greater than 2.16.0, specify it below.
    # You might also have to specify Python version supported by that version,
    # see https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/reference_appendices/release_and_maintenance.html#ansible-core-support-matrix
    # with:
    #   ansible-core-version: '2.17.0'
    #   python-versions: '["3.7", "3.8", "3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]'
    #   collection-root: 'ansible_collections/junipernetworks/junos'
    #   automation-hub: true
    # Uncomment the lines below if you have 'automation-hub: true' and need to install collections from Red Hat Ansible Automation Hub.
    # This requires setting a repository secret called 'AH_TOKEN' which value contains a Red Hat Ansible Automation Hub token.
    # secrets:
    #   AH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.AH_TOKEN }}

  sanity:
    name: Non-AAP Sanity (Ⓐ${{ matrix.ansible }})
    strategy:
      matrix:
        ansible:
          # Certification checks support the AAP ansible-core versions (2.16, 2.18, 2.20....)
          # This tests non-AAP versions
          - stable-2.19
          - stable-2.21
          - devel

    steps:
      - name: Perform sanity testing
        uses: ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action@release/v1
        with:
          ansible-core-version: ${{ matrix.ansible }}
          testing-type: sanity
          pull-request-change-detection: false
          coverage: never # coverage is always very low for sanity tests, and doesn't make much sense

  # This job does nothing and is only used for the branch protection
  # or multi-stage CI jobs, like making sure that all tests pass before
  # a publishing job is started.
  certification-check:
    if: always()

    needs:
      - sanity
      - certification_check

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Decide whether the needed jobs succeeded or failed
        uses: re-actors/alls-green@release/v1
        with:
          jobs: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}

  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - stable-*
  pull_request:

  schedule:

## SonarCloud analysis (fork-safe Pattern C)
#
# FLOW: Units completes (tests + coverage artifact, no SONAR_TOKEN) → workflow_run
# triggers this workflow on the default branch → finalize downloads coverage and scans.
#
# Reference: ansible-collections/amazon.aws (.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml)

---
name: SonarCloud

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows:
      - Units
    types:
      - completed

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  actions: read

jobs:
  publish-coverage:
    name: Publish Code Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    steps:
      # WARNING: Checking out the workflow_run.head_sha is potentially dangerous, as it may contain untrusted code.
      # Be careful when making changes to this workflow to ensure that code is not executed from the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          show-progress: false
          allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true

      - name: Download coverage artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          name: units-coverage

      - name: Set coverage report paths
        run: |
          coverage_files=$(find . -name "coverage*.xml" -type f 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//')
          echo "Found coverage files: ${coverage_files:-none}"
          echo "COVERAGE_PATHS=${coverage_files}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Get PR number and info
        if: github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          HEAD_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr list --head "$HEAD_BRANCH" --repo "$REPO" --json number -q '.[0].number')
          echo "PR_NUMBER=${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          if [[ -n "${PR_NUMBER}" ]]; then
            PR_DATA=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}")
            echo "PR_BASE=$(echo "$PR_DATA" | jq -r '.base.ref')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "PR_HEAD=$(echo "$PR_DATA" | jq -r '.head.ref')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      - name: Prepare SonarCloud args
        env:
          COMMIT_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          EVENT_TYPE: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.event }}
        run: |
          SONAR_ARGS="-Dsonar.scm.revision=\"${COMMIT_SHA}\""
          if [[ "${EVENT_TYPE}" == "pull_request" && -n "${PR_NUMBER:-}" ]]; then
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.pullrequest.key=${PR_NUMBER}"
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.pullrequest.branch=${PR_HEAD}"
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.pullrequest.base=${PR_BASE}"
          fi
          if [[ -n "${COVERAGE_PATHS:-}" ]]; then
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.python.coverage.reportPaths=${COVERAGE_PATHS}"
          fi
          echo "SONAR_ARGS=${SONAR_ARGS}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: SonarCloud Scan
        uses: SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action@d209202bc7d53ff1cc128f7f907dac145c9d6ae9
        env:
          SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_ORG_SONAR_TOKEN_CICD_BOT }}
        with:
          args: ${{ env.SONAR_ARGS }}

on:

    branches:
      - main
      - stable-*
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: >-

      github.event.pull_request.number || github.sha
    }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  integration-matrix:
    name: Build integration target matrix
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      target_groups: ${{ steps.set-matrix.outputs.target_groups }}
    steps:
      # ansible-test requires the collection to live at
      # <root>/ansible_collections/<namespace>/<name>/, and its change
      # detection needs full git history plus a local base branch to diff
      # against, so check out there with fetch-depth 0.
      - name: Checkout repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          path: ansible_collections/vmware/vmware_rest
          fetch-depth: 0
          # For pull requests, check out the branch head (not the merge commit)
          # so change detection sees a normal feature branch forked from base.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      - name: Install python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install ansible-core
        run: python -m pip install ansible-core

      - id: select-targets
        name: Select affected integration targets
        working-directory: ansible_collections/vmware/vmware_rest
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config --global --add safe.directory "$PWD"

          run_all=false
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" != "pull_request" ]; then
            # Pushes land on an "official" branch (main / stable-*) which
            # ansible-test refuses to run change detection against, so run the
            # full suite.
            run_all=true
          elif git diff --name-only "origin/${BASE_REF}...HEAD" | grep -q '^\.github/'; then
            # ansible-test does not model .github/ changes; run everything so CI
            # changes are validated against the whole suite.
            echo "Detected .github/ changes; running all targets."
            run_all=true
          fi

          # ansible-test writes the target list to stdout and diagnostics
          # (detected branch, changed files, warnings) to stderr; keep stderr in
          # the job log for debugging while capturing only targets to the file.
          if [ "$run_all" = "true" ]; then
            # List every target ansible-test knows about (no change detection).
            ansible-test integration --list-targets > targets.txt
          else
            # Recreate the base branch locally and run ansible-test change
            # detection to map the diff to affected integration targets.
            git branch -f "$BASE_REF" "origin/${BASE_REF}"
            git checkout -B "pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >/dev/null 2>&1
            ansible-test integration --list-targets --changed \
              --base-branch "$BASE_REF" > targets.txt
          fi

          echo "Candidate targets:"
          cat targets.txt

      - id: set-matrix
        name: Filter targets and split into groups of 10
        working-directory: ansible_collections/vmware/vmware_rest
        run: |
          python <<'EOF'
          import json
          import os
          from pathlib import Path

          group_size = 10

          # vmware_rest_* are live-vCenter scenario targets that do not run
          # against the mock server, and prepare_* are hidden setup helpers;
          # exclude both from the mock integration matrix.
          targets = sorted(
              line.strip()
              for line in Path("targets.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
              if line.strip()
              and not line.strip().startswith("vmware_rest_")
              and not line.strip().startswith("prepare_")
          )

          target_groups = [
              {
                  "id": (index // group_size) + 1,
                  "targets": " ".join(targets[index : index + group_size]),
              }
              for index in range(0, len(targets), group_size)
          ]

          print(f"Selected {len(targets)} target(s) in {len(target_groups)} group(s).")

          with open(os.environ["GITHUB_OUTPUT"], "a", encoding="utf-8") as output:
              output.write(f"target_groups={json.dumps(target_groups)}\n")
          EOF

  integration:
    name: Integration (Ⓐ${{ matrix.versions.ansible }} - ${{ matrix.versions.python }} - group ${{ matrix.target_group.id }})
    needs: integration-matrix
    # Skip cleanly when no targets are affected. An empty matrix vector is a hard
    # error in GitHub Actions (not a skip), so guard the whole job instead.
    if: ${{ needs.integration-matrix.outputs.target_groups != '[]' }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        target_group: ${{ fromJSON(needs.integration-matrix.outputs.target_groups) }}
        versions:
          # Testing all ansible-core and controller Python versions is impractical. Only test the
          # newest and oldest controller Python versions supported by each ansible-core we support.
          # https://endoflife.date/ansible-core (Control node Python column)
          # Add publish_coverage: true to the version you want to publish coverage for, usually latest.
          - { python: "3.14", ansible: stable-2.21 }
          - { python: "3.12", ansible: stable-2.21 }
          - { python: "3.14", ansible: stable-2.20, publish_coverage: true }
          - { python: "3.12", ansible: stable-2.20 }
          - { python: "3.13", ansible: stable-2.19 }
          - { python: "3.11", ansible: stable-2.19 }
          - { python: "3.12", ansible: stable-2.16 }
          - { python: "3.10", ansible: stable-2.16 }

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Update podman
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          sudo apt-get update -y
          sudo apt-get install -y --upgrade podman crun

      - name: Checkout repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.versions.python }}

      - name: Install ansible-core
        run: |
          python -m pip install https://github.com/ansible/ansible/archive/${{ matrix.versions.ansible }}.tar.gz;

      - name: Install collection and python requirements
        run: |
          ansible-galaxy collection install . --force;

      - name: Perform integration tests
        run: |
          make integration INTEGRATION_TARGETS="${{ matrix.target_group.targets }}";

  # This job does nothing and is only used for the branch protection
  # or multi-stage CI jobs, like making sure that all tests pass before
  # a publishing job is started.
  integration-check:
    if: always()
    needs:
      - integration
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether the needed jobs succeeded or failed
        uses: re-actors/alls-green@release/v1
        with:
          # When no targets are affected by a change the integration job has an
          # empty matrix and is skipped; that must not fail the check.
          allowed-skips: integration
          jobs: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}

#
# FLOW: Units completes (tests + coverage artifact, no SONAR_TOKEN) → workflow_run

  contents: read

jobs:
  publish-coverage:
    name: Publish Code Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    steps:
      # WARNING: Checking out the workflow_run.head_sha is potentially dangerous, as it may contain untrusted code.
      # Be careful when making changes to this workflow to ensure that code is not executed from the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          show-progress: false
          allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true

      - name: Download coverage artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          name: units-coverage

      - name: Set coverage report paths
        run: |
          coverage_files=$(find . -name "coverage*.xml" -type f 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//')
          echo "Found coverage files: ${coverage_files:-none}"
          echo "COVERAGE_PATHS=${coverage_files}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Get PR number and info
        if: github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          HEAD_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr list --head "$HEAD_BRANCH" --repo "$REPO" --json number -q '.[0].number')
          echo "PR_NUMBER=${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          if [[ -n "${PR_NUMBER}" ]]; then
            PR_DATA=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}")
            echo "PR_BASE=$(echo "$PR_DATA" | jq -r '.base.ref')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "PR_HEAD=$(echo "$PR_DATA" | jq -r '.head.ref')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      - name: Prepare SonarCloud args
        env:
          COMMIT_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          EVENT_TYPE: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.event }}
        run: |
          SONAR_ARGS="-Dsonar.scm.revision=\"${COMMIT_SHA}\""
          if [[ "${EVENT_TYPE}" == "pull_request" && -n "${PR_NUMBER:-}" ]]; then
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.pullrequest.key=${PR_NUMBER}"
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.pullrequest.branch=${PR_HEAD}"
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.pullrequest.base=${PR_BASE}"
          fi
          if [[ -n "${COVERAGE_PATHS:-}" ]]; then
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.python.coverage.reportPaths=${COVERAGE_PATHS}"
          fi
          echo "SONAR_ARGS=${SONAR_ARGS}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: SonarCloud Scan
        uses: SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action@d209202bc7d53ff1cc128f7f907dac145c9d6ae9
        env:
          SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_ORG_SONAR_TOKEN_CICD_BOT }}
        with:
          args: ${{ env.SONAR_ARGS }}

    ${{ github.workflow }}-${{
      github.event.pull_request.number || github.sha
    }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  ###
  # Sanity tests (REQUIRED)
  #
  # https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/dev_guide/testing_sanity.html

  sanity:
    name: Sanity (Ⓐ${{ matrix.ansible }})
    strategy:
      matrix:
        ansible:
          # It's important that Sanity is tested against all stable-X.Y branches
          # Testing against `devel` may fail as new tests are added.
          # An alternative to `devel` is the `milestone` branch with
          # gets synchronized with `devel` every few weeks and therefore
          # tends to be a more stable target. Be aware that it is not updated
          # around creation of a new stable branch, this might cause a problem
          # that two different versions of ansible-test use the same sanity test
          # ignore.txt file.
          # Add new versions announced in
          # https://github.com/ansible-collections/news-for-maintainers in a timely manner,
          # consider dropping testing against EOL versions and versions you don't support.
          - stable-2.16
          - stable-2.17
          - stable-2.18
          - stable-2.19
          - devel
        # - milestone
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Run sanity tests inside a Docker container.
      # The docker container has all the pinned dependencies that are
      # required and all Python versions Ansible supports.
      - name: Perform sanity testing
        # See the documentation for the following GitHub action on
        # https://github.com/ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action/blob/main/README.md
        uses: ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action@release/v1
        with:
          ansible-core-version: ${{ matrix.ansible }}
          testing-type: sanity
          # OPTIONAL If your sanity tests require code
          # from other collections, install them like this
          # test-deps: >-
          #   ansible.netcommon
          #   ansible.utils
          # OPTIONAL If set to true, will test only against changed files,
          # which should improve CI performance. See limitations on
          # https://github.com/ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action#pull-request-change-detection
          pull-request-change-detection: false
          coverage: never # coverage is always very low for sanity tests, and doesn't make much sense

  # This job does nothing and is only used for the branch protection
  # or multi-stage CI jobs, like making sure that all tests pass before
  # a publishing job is started.
  sanity-check:
    if: always()

    needs:
      - sanity

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Decide whether the needed jobs succeeded or failed
        uses: re-actors/alls-green@release/v1
        with:
          jobs: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}

---
name: Ansible Test
on:

  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

  schedule:
    - cron: '0 0 * * 0'  # Every Sunday at midnight UTC

  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      targets:
        description: >-
          Integration test targets to run (space-separated, e.g. "win_scom_alert win_scom_alert_info").
          Leave empty to run ALL targets.
        required: false
        default: ""

concurrency:
  group: >-
    ${{ github.workflow }}-${{
      github.event.pull_request.number || github.sha
    }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  # Approve protected environment once instead of once per job in the matrix.
  # detect-changes depends on this so no PR code runs before a maintainer approves.
  # Skipped for schedule/workflow_dispatch runs on the base branch (main) — no untrusted
  # code is involved, so the approval gate is not needed. All other eco-scom environment
  # restrictions (secrets scoping, deployment protection rules) remain in place.
  approve:
    name: Approve Integration
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: eco-scom
    steps:
      - run: echo "Deployment approved"

  # Determine which integration test targets need to run based on changed files.
  # To associate a module_utils file with a specific integration target, name it
  # _<PascalCase>Utils.psm1 — e.g. _RunAsDistributionUtils.psm1 → win_scom_run_as_distribution.
  detect-changes:
    name: Detect Changed Modules
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [approve]
    if: >-
      always() &&
      (needs.approve.result == 'success' ||
       github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
       github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    outputs:
      cli_args: ${{ steps.targets.outputs.cli_args }}
      has_targets: ${{ steps.targets.outputs.has_targets }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true

      - name: Determine integration test targets
        id: targets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
            # Manual trigger → use provided targets or fall back to ALL
            if [[ -n "${{ github.event.inputs.targets }}" ]]; then
              TARGETS="${{ github.event.inputs.targets }}"
            else
              TARGETS="ALL"
            fi
          elif [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "schedule" ]]; then
            # Scheduled run → always run ALL tests as safety net
            TARGETS="ALL"
          else
            # pull_request_target → selective based on changed files
            BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
            HEAD_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
            git fetch origin "${BASE_SHA}" 2>/dev/null || true
            git fetch origin "${HEAD_SHA}" 2>/dev/null || true
            CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "${BASE_SHA}...${HEAD_SHA}")
            echo "Changed files:"
            echo "${CHANGED:-  (none)}"

            # ---------------------------------------------------------------
            # Inlined target-detection logic (was: scripts/get_integration_targets.sh)
            #
            # Mapping rules:
            #   plugins/modules/<name>.ps1|.yml        → win_scom_<name>
            #   plugins/modules/<name>_info.ps1|.yml   → win_scom_<name>  (strip _info suffix)
            #   plugins/module_utils/_<Pascal>Utils.psm1
            #       → derive target: strip leading _ and Utils.psm1 suffix,
            #         convert PascalCase to snake_case, prepend win_scom_
            #       → if tests/integration/targets/win_scom_<snake> exists → run that target only
            #       → otherwise (shared/general utils, e.g. _SCOMPsSetupUtils.psm1) → ALL
            #   plugins/module_utils/<other>           → ALL win_scom_* targets
            #   tests/integration/targets/win_scom_*   → win_scom_<name>
            # ---------------------------------------------------------------
            MODULES_DIR="plugins/modules"
            MODULE_UTILS_DIR="plugins/module_utils"
            INTEGRATION_DIR="tests/integration/targets"
            targets=""
            run_all=false

            while IFS= read -r file; do
              [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

              # module_utils change: try to map _<Pascal>Utils.psm1 → specific target
              if [[ "$file" == "${MODULE_UTILS_DIR}/"* ]]; then
                utils_file=$(basename "$file")
                # Match the naming convention: _<PascalCase>Utils.psm1
                if [[ "$utils_file" == _*Utils.psm1 ]]; then
                  pascal_name="${utils_file#_}"             # strip leading _
                  pascal_name="${pascal_name%Utils.psm1}"  # strip Utils.psm1 suffix
                  # Convert PascalCase → snake_case:
                  #   insert _ before each uppercase letter, lowercase all, strip leading _
                  snake_name=$(echo "$pascal_name" \
                    | sed 's/\([A-Z]\)/_\1/g' \
                    | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' \
                    | sed 's/^_//')
                  target="win_scom_${snake_name}"
                  if [[ -d "${INTEGRATION_DIR}/${target}" ]]; then
                    # Dedicated integration target found → run only that target
                    if [[ " ${targets} " != *" ${target} "* ]]; then
                      targets="${targets:+${targets} }${target}"
                    fi
                    continue
                  fi
                fi
                # No dedicated target (shared/general utils) → run ALL
                run_all=true
                break
              fi

              # Module source file changed (.ps1 or .yml)
              if [[ "$file" == "${MODULES_DIR}/"*.ps1 || "$file" == "${MODULES_DIR}/"*.yml ]]; then
                filename=$(basename "$file")
                module_name="${filename%.*}"       # strip extension
                base_name="${module_name%_info}"   # strip _info suffix
                target="win_scom_${base_name}"
                if [[ -d "${INTEGRATION_DIR}/${target}" ]] && \
                   [[ " ${targets} " != *" ${target} "* ]]; then
                  targets="${targets:+${targets} }${target}"
                fi
                continue
              fi

              # Integration test file changed directly
              if [[ "$file" == "${INTEGRATION_DIR}/win_scom_"* ]]; then
                rel="${file#"${INTEGRATION_DIR}/"}"
                target="${rel%%/*}"
                if [[ -d "${INTEGRATION_DIR}/${target}" ]] && \
                   [[ " ${targets} " != *" ${target} "* ]]; then
                  targets="${targets:+${targets} }${target}"
                fi
                continue
              fi

            done <<< "${CHANGED}"

            if [[ "$run_all" == "true" ]]; then
              TARGETS="ALL"
            else
              TARGETS="${targets}"
            fi
          fi

          echo "Integration targets: ${TARGETS:-none}"

          if [[ "${TARGETS}" == "ALL" ]]; then
            # module_utils changed → run all tests, no target filter
            echo "cli_args=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "has_targets=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [[ -n "${TARGETS// /}" ]]; then
            # Specific targets changed
            echo "cli_args=${TARGETS}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "has_targets=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            # No relevant files changed → skip integration entirely
            echo "cli_args=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "has_targets=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  integration:
    runs-on: [self-hosted]
    needs:
      - approve
      - detect-changes
    # Skip entirely when no relevant files changed.
    # For schedule/workflow_dispatch the approve gate is intentionally skipped —
    # use an explicit allowlist so any future trigger addition cannot silently bypass it.
    if: >-
      always() &&
      (needs.approve.result == 'success' ||
       github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
       github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_targets == 'true'
    name: I (Ⓐ${{ matrix.ansible }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 1
      matrix:
        # Add new versions announced in
        # https://github.com/ansible-collections/news-for-maintainers in a timely manner,
        # consider dropping testing against EOL versions and versions you don't support.
        include:
          - ansible: devel
            python: 3.13
          - ansible: stable-2.16
            python: 3.12
          - ansible: stable-2.17
            python: 3.12
          - ansible: stable-2.18
            python: 3.12
          - ansible: stable-2.19
            python: 3.12
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true

      - name: Install python
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          if ! command -v python${{ matrix.python }}; then
            sudo dnf install -y \
              python${{ matrix.python }} \
              python${{ matrix.python }}-pip
          fi

      - name: Run integration tests
        run: |
          python${{ matrix.python }} -m venv .venv
          source .venv/bin/activate
          pip install https://github.com/ansible/ansible/archive/${{ matrix.ansible }}.tar.gz
          make integration \
            ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_PATH="${{ github.workspace }}" \
            CLI_ARGS="${{ needs.detect-changes.outputs.cli_args }}"
        env:
          ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_PATH: "${{ github.workspace }}"
          SCOM_HOSTNAME: ${{ secrets.SCOM_HOSTNAME }}
          SCOM_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.SCOM_USERNAME }}
          SCOM_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.SCOM_PASSWORD }}

      - name: Clean up
        if: always()
        run: |
          rm -rf ./*

  check: # This job does nothing and is only used for the branch protection
    # or multi-stage CI jobs, like making sure that all tests pass before
    # a publishing job is started.
    if: always()

    needs:
      - integration

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Decide whether the needed jobs succeeded or failed
        uses: re-actors/alls-green@release/v1
        with:
          # Allow integration to be skipped when no relevant files changed
          allowed-skips: integration
          jobs: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}

on:

    types:
      - opened

name: Collection Docs (PR)
concurrency:
  group: docs-pr-${{ github.head_ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
"on":
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, closed]

env:
  GHP_BASE_URL: https://${{ github.repository_owner }}.github.io/${{ github.event.repository.name }}

jobs:
  # Validation job runs a strict build to ensure it will fail CI on any mistakes.
  validate-docs:
    permissions:
      contents: read
    name: Validate Ansible Docs
    if: github.event.action != 'closed'
    uses: ansible-community/github-docs-build/.github/workflows/_shared-docs-build-push.yml@main
    with:
      artifact-upload: false
      init-lenient: false
      init-fail-on-error: true
      build-ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.number }}/merge

  # The build job runs with the most lenient settings to ensure the best chance of getting
  # a rendered docsite that can be looked at.
  build-docs:
    permissions:
      contents: read
    name: Build Ansible Docs
    uses: ansible-community/github-docs-build/.github/workflows/_shared-docs-build-pr.yml@main
    with:
      init-lenient: true
      init-fail-on-error: false

  comment:
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-docs]
    name: PR comments
    steps:
      - name: PR comment
        uses: ansible-community/github-docs-build/actions/ansible-docs-build-comment@main
        with:
          body-includes: "## Docs Build"
          reactions: heart
          action: ${{ needs.build-docs.outputs.changed != 'true' && 'remove' || '' }}
          on-closed-action: remove
          on-merged-action: remove
          body: |
            ## Docs Build 📝

            Thank you for contribution!✨

            The docsite for **this PR** is available for download as an artifact from this run:
            ${{ needs.build-docs.outputs.artifact-url }}

            You can compare to the docs for the `main` branch here:
            ${{ env.GHP_BASE_URL }}/branch/main

            File changes:

            ${{ needs.build-docs.outputs.diff-files-rendered }}

            ${{ needs.build-docs.outputs.diff-rendered }}

name: Collection Docs (Publish)
concurrency:
  group: docs-push-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
"on":
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    tags:
      - "*"
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 13 * * *"

jobs:
  build-docs:
    permissions:
      contents: read
    name: Build Ansible Docs
    uses: ansible-community/github-docs-build/.github/workflows/_shared-docs-build-push.yml@main
    with:
      init-lenient: false
      init-fail-on-error: true

  publish-docs-gh-pages:
    # use to prevent running on forks
    if: github.repository == 'ansible-collections/microsoft.scom'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    needs: [build-docs]
    name: Publish Ansible Docs
    uses: ansible-community/github-docs-build/.github/workflows/_shared-docs-build-publish-gh-pages.yml@main
    with:
      artifact-name: ${{ needs.build-docs.outputs.artifact-name }}
      publish-gh-pages-branch: true
    secrets:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

## SonarCloud analysis (fork-safe Pattern C)
#
# FLOW: Units completes (tests + coverage artifact, no SONAR_TOKEN) → workflow_run
# triggers this workflow on the default branch → finalize downloads coverage and scans.
#
# Reference: ansible-collections/amazon.aws (.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml)

---
name: SonarCloud

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows:
      - unit tests
    types:
      - completed

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  actions: read

jobs:
  publish-coverage:
    name: Publish Code Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    steps:
      # WARNING: Checking out the workflow_run.head_sha is potentially dangerous, as it may contain untrusted code.
      # Be careful when making changes to this workflow to ensure that code is not executed from the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          show-progress: false
          allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true

      - name: Download coverage artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          name: units-coverage

      - name: Set coverage report paths
        run: |
          coverage_files=$(find . -name "coverage*.xml" -type f 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//')
          echo "Found coverage files: ${coverage_files:-none}"
          echo "COVERAGE_PATHS=${coverage_files}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Get PR number and info
        if: github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          HEAD_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr list --head "$HEAD_BRANCH" --repo "$REPO" --json number -q '.[0].number')
          echo "PR_NUMBER=${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          if [[ -n "${PR_NUMBER}" ]]; then
            PR_DATA=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}")
            echo "PR_BASE=$(echo "$PR_DATA" | jq -r '.base.ref')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "PR_HEAD=$(echo "$PR_DATA" | jq -r '.head.ref')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      - name: Prepare SonarCloud args
        env:
          COMMIT_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          EVENT_TYPE: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.event }}
        run: |
          SONAR_ARGS="-Dsonar.scm.revision=\"${COMMIT_SHA}\""
          if [[ "${EVENT_TYPE}" == "pull_request" && -n "${PR_NUMBER:-}" ]]; then
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.pullrequest.key=${PR_NUMBER}"
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.pullrequest.branch=${PR_HEAD}"
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.pullrequest.base=${PR_BASE}"
          fi
          if [[ -n "${COVERAGE_PATHS:-}" ]]; then
            SONAR_ARGS="${SONAR_ARGS} -Dsonar.python.coverage.reportPaths=${COVERAGE_PATHS}"
          fi
          echo "SONAR_ARGS=${SONAR_ARGS}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: SonarCloud Scan
        uses: SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action@d209202bc7d53ff1cc128f7f907dac145c9d6ae9
        env:
          SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_ORG_SONAR_TOKEN_CICD_BOT }}
        with:
          args: ${{ env.SONAR_ARGS }}

    - cron: '0 6 * * *'

concurrency:
  group: >-
    ${{ github.workflow }}-${{
      github.event.pull_request.number || github.sha
    }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:

###
# Sanity tests (REQUIRED)
#
# https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/dev_guide/testing_sanity.html

  sanity:
    name: Sanity (Ⓐ${{ matrix.ansible }})
    strategy:
      matrix:
        ansible:
          # It's important that Sanity is tested against all stable-X.Y branches
          # Testing against `devel` may fail as new tests are added.
          # An alternative to `devel` is the `milestone` branch with
          # gets synchronized with `devel` every few weeks and therefore
          # tends to be a more stable target. Be aware that it is not updated
          # around creation of a new stable branch, this might cause a problem
          # that two different versions of ansible-test use the same sanity test
          # ignore.txt file.
          # Add new versions announced in
          # https://github.com/ansible-collections/news-for-maintainers in a timely manner,
          # consider dropping testing against EOL versions and versions you don't support.
          - stable-2.18
          - stable-2.19
          - stable-2.20
          - stable-2.21
          - devel
        # - milestone

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Run sanity tests inside a Docker container.
      # The docker container has all the pinned dependencies that are
      # required and all Python versions Ansible supports.
      - name: Perform sanity testing
        # See the documentation for the following GitHub action on
        # https://github.com/ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action/blob/main/README.md
        uses: ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action@release/v1
        with:
          ansible-core-version: ${{ matrix.ansible }}
          testing-type: sanity
          # codecov-token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          # OPTIONAL If your sanity tests require code
          # from other collections, install them like this
          test-deps: >-
            ansible.windows
          # OPTIONAL If set to true, will test only against changed files,
          # which should improve CI performance. See limitations on
          # https://github.com/ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action#pull-request-change-detection
          pull-request-change-detection: false

###
# Unit tests (OPTIONAL)
#
# https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/dev_guide/testing_units.html

  units:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    name: Units (Ⓐ${{ matrix.ansible }})
    strategy:
      # As soon as the first unit test fails, cancel the others to free up the CI queue
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        ansible:
          # Add new versions announced in
          # https://github.com/ansible-collections/news-for-maintainers in a timely manner,
          # consider dropping testing against EOL versions and versions you don't support.
          - stable-2.18
          - stable-2.19
          - stable-2.20
          - stable-2.21
          - devel
        # - milestone

    steps:
      - name: >-
          Perform unit testing against
          Ansible version ${{ matrix.ansible }}
        # See the documentation for the following GitHub action on
        # https://github.com/ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action/blob/main/README.md
        uses: ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action@release/v1
        with:
          ansible-core-version: ${{ matrix.ansible }}
          testing-type: units
          # codecov-token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          # OPTIONAL If your unit tests require code
          # from other collections, install them like this
          test-deps: >-
            ansible.windows
          # OPTIONAL If set to true, will test only against changed files,
          # which should improve CI performance. See limitations on
          # https://github.com/ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action#pull-request-change-detection
          pull-request-change-detection: false

###
# Integration tests (RECOMMENDED)
#
# https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/dev_guide/testing_integration.html


# If the application you are testing is available as a docker container and you want to test
# multiple versions see the following for an example:
# https://github.com/ansible-collections/community.zabbix/tree/master/.github/workflows

  integration:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    name: I (Ⓐ${{ matrix.ansible }}+py${{ matrix.python }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        ansible:
          - devel
        # - milestone
        python:
          - '3.9'
          - '3.10'
          - '3.11'
          - '3.12'
          - '3.13'
          - '3.14'
        include:
          # Add new versions announced in
          # https://github.com/ansible-collections/news-for-maintainers in a timely manner,
          # consider dropping testing against EOL versions and versions you don't support.
          # ansible-core 2.18
          - ansible: stable-2.18
            python: '3.8'
          - ansible: stable-2.18
            python: '3.9'
          - ansible: stable-2.18
            python: '3.10'
          - ansible: stable-2.18
            python: '3.11'
          - ansible: stable-2.18
            python: '3.12'
          - ansible: stable-2.18
            python: '3.13'
          # ansible-core 2.19
          - ansible: stable-2.19
            python: '3.8'
          - ansible: stable-2.19
            python: '3.9'
          - ansible: stable-2.19
            python: '3.10'
          - ansible: stable-2.19
            python: '3.11'
          - ansible: stable-2.19
            python: '3.12'
          - ansible: stable-2.19
            python: '3.13'
          # ansible-core 2.20
          - ansible: stable-2.20
            python: '3.9'
          - ansible: stable-2.20
            python: '3.10'
          - ansible: stable-2.20
            python: '3.11'
          - ansible: stable-2.20
            python: '3.12'
          - ansible: stable-2.20
            python: '3.13'
          - ansible: stable-2.20
            python: '3.14'
          # ansible-core 2.21
          - ansible: stable-2.21
            python: '3.10'
          - ansible: stable-2.21
            python: '3.11'
          - ansible: stable-2.21
            python: '3.12'
          - ansible: stable-2.21
            python: '3.13'
          - ansible: stable-2.21
            python: '3.14'


    steps:
      - name: >-
          Perform integration testing against
          Ansible version ${{ matrix.ansible }}
          under Python ${{ matrix.python }}
        # See the documentation for the following GitHub action on
        # https://github.com/ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action/blob/main/README.md
        uses: ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action@release/v1
        with:
          ansible-core-version: ${{ matrix.ansible }}
          # OPTIONAL command to run before invoking `ansible-test integration`
          # pre-test-cmd:
          target-python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
          testing-type: integration
          # codecov-token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          # OPTIONAL If your integration tests require code
          # from other collections, install them like this
          test-deps: ansible.windows
          # OPTIONAL If set to true, will test only against changed files,
          # which should improve CI performance. See limitations on
          # https://github.com/ansible-community/ansible-test-gh-action#pull-request-change-detection
          pull-request-change-detection: false


  check:  # This job does nothing and is only used for the branch protection
          # or multi-stage CI jobs, like making sure that all tests pass before
          # a publishing job is started.
    if: always()

    needs:
      - sanity
      - units
      - integration

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Decide whether the needed jobs succeeded or failed
        uses: re-actors/alls-green@release/v1
        with:
          jobs: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}

name: Run collection certification checks

permissions:
  contents: read

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * *"

concurrency:
  group: cert-ver-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  call:
    uses: ansible-collections/partner-certification-checker/.github/workflows/certification-reusable.yml@v4.0.0

---
name: Lint extra docsite docs and links
on:
  # Run CI against all pushes (direct commits, also merged PRs), Pull Requests
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - stable-*
  pull_request:
  # Run CI once per day (at 06:00 UTC)
  # This ensures that even if there haven't been commits that we are still testing against latest version of ansible-test for each ansible-base version
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * *'

jobs:
  docsite:
    name: Lint extra docsite docs and links
    permissions:
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:

      - name: Check out code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v3
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      - name: Install ansible-core and antsibull-docs
        run: pip install ansible-core antsibull-docs --disable-pip-version-check

      - name: Install dependent collections
        run: ansible-galaxy collection install ansible.windows

      - name: Run collection docs linter
        run: antsibull-docs lint-collection-docs . --plugin-docs --skip-rstcheck
